1) SCFAs absorption was enhanced in non-lactating cows fed 60% concentrates compared to cows fed forage-only; 2) the absorption was more enhanced by the continuous feeding of 60% concentrates than by the interrupted feeding; 3) lactate was absorbed from the reticulomunen of non-lactationg cows fed 60 % concentrates.

1) the absorption rates of total SCFAs and acetate across the reticulum were enhanced by the 60% concentrate-feeding for 4 wk, and 2) the lactate was not absorbed across the reticulo-rumen during the baseline (forage-only diet), but after the 60% concentrates feeding for 4 wk.

the in vivo absorption of acetate, propionic and butyric acids was significantly enhanced by continuous high-concentrate feeding, while that of lactate was enhanced by both continuous and interrupted high-concentrate diets.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the continuous feeding strategy of high concentrate diets seems to be more beneficial in terms of ruminal acidosis prevention and energy supply compared to the interrupted strategy.

the reticulomuninal absorption of SCFA was higher after continuous concentrate feeding compared to interrupted feeding and lactate was absorbed from the reticulrumen after both continuous and intermittent feeding of concentrate.
lactate absorption across reticuloruminant epithelium is a physiological process that is enhanced by high concentrate feeding in non-lactating cows.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the continuous feeding of high concentrate levels is more beneficial for rumen acidosis protection than the interrupted feeding of high concentrate.
the reticuloreminal SCFA absorption is enhanced by the 60% concentrate diet, and that this absorption is further enhanced when the diet is fed in a continuous manner.
the reticuloreminal absorption of SCFA is enhanced by continuous feeding of concentrates, while lactate absorption is enhanced by both continuous and interrupted feeding of concentrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the absorption of SCF and lactate across the reticulum of non-lactatng cows can be enhanced by continuous feeding of high concentrate diets, but not by interrupted feeding.
the reticuloreminal absorption of SCFA can be enhanced by continuous high concentrate feeding.
the continuous high concentrate feeding is more advantageous in terms preventing rumen acidosis and enhancing SCFA absorption than the interrupted feeding model.
